Title: High-severity ticket pages on-call inside SLA window
Given: a ticket arrives via one of the documented support channels
When: the triage flow assigns severity High
Then: the on-call agent receives a page AND the initial response lands within <= 240 minutes of ticket arrival
Notes: Asserts NFR-PERF-001 first-response-minutes target literally (<= 240). Paging behavior derives from C-003.

Title: Engineering escalation captures reproduction steps
Given: a Triage Agent has identified a ticket for engineering escalation
When: the agent escalates the ticket to engineering
Then: the escalation carries reproduction steps so the half-business-day slowdown observed in C-006 does not recur
Notes: Manual scenario; observability is presence of repro steps at handoff to engineering, not a specific UI control.

Title: Duplicate-suspect signal surfaces at intake prior to agent pickup
Given: an incoming ticket is processed by the intake pipeline
When: the intake pipeline runs near-duplicate detection prior to agent pickup
Then: a duplicate-suspect signal surfaces before agent pickup so the approximately 15% post-claim duplicate rate from C-005 decreases
Notes: Automation deferred — duplicate-rate baseline against ticketing-system data open per A51-001.
